sense.text:
We’re going to talk about the thousand year reign, only the first five verses of Revelation 20, but before that we open with Leviticus 26.

“But if ye will not hearken unto me, and will not do all these commandments”: the issue has always been the Most High’s commandments, from Genesis to Revelation. That has always been the problem and that has always been the solution. You don’t read about religious denominations in the Bible; they don’t exist in the Bible. What exists is the commandments.

Wherever we go people ask us what the true religion of God is. The commandments, that’s what it is. The word religion comes from a Greek word, religio, which means to hold back, keep down and restrain. God’s commandments teach us to hold back, keep down and restrain ourselves from worshiping idols, dishonoring our parents, killing, stealing. That is the religion of the Bible: the commandments.

“But that ye break my covenant: I also will do this unto you; I will even appoint over you terror, consumption”: for breaking God’s laws he said he will appoint terror over us. “And ye shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.”

“And I will set my face against you”: God said he will set his face against us. “And ye shall be slain before your enemies”, and we have been slain. The murders this year, the killings by police and by white folks, put them on the screen; the images, Trayvon Martin and the others. It’s so easy: go to Google, type it in, it takes four seconds. “They that hate you shall reign over you.”

“And ye shall flee when none pursueth you”: that’s not just here in America, that’s in many of our other lands too. An article from Al Jazeera: the European Union is responsible for slavery in Libya. Its migration policies have resulted in slavery conditions for migrants in Libya, and the migrants they’re talking about are our people throughout the continent of Africa, sold into slavery. Brothers and sisters thought slavery was over. It is not over. None of us are free so long as one of us is kept: that’s the mentality all of us must have, because if it happens to them over there it can surely happen to us over here. Nobody’s doing nothing about it. No churches are speaking about it, the Nation of Islam ain’t speaking about it, they ain’t doing a damn thing. We’re the only ones talking about this thing.

In 2017 slave markets were found along the North African migrant routes, where hundreds of young African men were being tormented. So the Arabs are going to get it too; it ain’t just the white man. All of those Arab families, every last one of them. Black men were being sold by an auctioneer for the equivalent of eight hundred dollars. Y’all think this is a joke; it ain’t no joke, it’s real. Sisters out there that want to travel by yourselves, so independent: you get caught up in this thing and you find out you ain’t independent. There were demonstrations, the African Union and the presidents demanded prosecutions, Libya said it would investigate. That is all BS, all just talk.

The next article is dated April 17, 2023: enslavement of African migrants is big business in Libya thanks to EU funding. The first article was years ago and nothing was done; this year they’re still talking about it. We ain’t got time to argue about a corner they don’t own while people are being sold into slavery. In 2017 they said they were going to investigate, and a three-year investigation by the United Nations found arbitrary detention, murder, rape, enslavement, sexual slavery, extrajudicial killing and enforced disappearance to be a widespread practice. You can’t make this stuff up.

Libya was once prosperous, and NATO plunged it into civil war with its regime change war; that’s why they got rid of Gaddafi. The European Union is the economic side and NATO is the military side, and they keep Africa destabilized. There’s always a war, there’s always a coup. Our people there say we need a better life, and try to go to Europe for jobs and education. They know that when our people go towards European countries they go through Arab countries and get caught up in slavery that America and NATO have funded, financially and militarily. The European Union outsourced the dirty work to the Libyan Coast Guard, and the migrants are sent back to Libya, to official and secret prisons, exploited through forced labor, ransom and sexual slavery.

So go back to what God said in the time of Moses. The Lord was not playing with our people. We thought it all ended; our people over there say we escaped slavery. The Lord said no, you didn’t.
“If ye will not yet for all this hearken unto me, then I will punish you seven times more for your sins.” He would punish us seven times more for our sins.
“And I will break the pride of your power”: that’s why we have no power today. “And I will make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass”: that’s slavery also.
“And your strength shall be spent in vain: for your land shall not yield her increase, neither shall the trees of the land yield their fruits.” This is the drought, the land not giving its increase.

precepts.why:
Same chapter, jump down: “And yet for all that, when they be in the land of their enemies”. In the land of our enemies, like we’re in America, and our people on the continent of Africa going out through Europe and getting taken to Libya, places like that. And it’s not just Libya; there are other articles about Afghanistan and other Arab nations doing the same thing, Saudi Arabia included. Remember Janet Jackson married an Arab man and had a baby by him; she ran back to America and never explained her story, never said what happened over there. Just think about that.

“I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”: God said he would not cast us away, neither would he hate us to destroy all of us totally. “And to break my covenant with them: for I am the Lord their God.” He would not break his covenant with the Israelites. He’s the Lord our God.

“But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”: highlight that word ancestors. Christianity teaches that ancestry has no place in the Bible. It’s right there. Our ancestry is very important. And if you don’t know your ancestors, don’t worry about it; faith supersedes that. That’s what the Lord promised, that’s what he prophesied: “whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the heathen, that I might be their God: I am the Lord.”

sense.text:
What did the Lord say about slavery? The Arabs think they’re escaping, like the white man thinks he’s going to escape, and our own people who kidnap our sisters think they’re going to escape too. They ain’t going to escape.

“And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.” That’s God’s law for the worldwide, that law is for everybody. The other nations do worse than what our own people do, and this is the judgment on them.

This is why they say don’t read the Old Testament: you might stumble across Exodus 21:16 in church and say, wait a minute, John Hagee, Joel Osteen, Kenneth Copeland, even the black ones, TD Jakes, can you explain this law? Oh no, you ain’t got to read that. They said don’t read the Old Testament because you might come across judgments that are going to affect their white constituents.

precepts.why:
There’s a little precept there. This is the law for our people, and for those out there touching our young daughters and trying to sell them throughout Atlanta, throughout Georgia, New York City, wherever they’re at. Here’s the law: “If a man be found stealing any of his brethren of the children of Israel, and maketh merchandise of him, or selleth him; then that thief shall die”. That’s what God says. “And thou shalt put evil away from among you.”

That’s God’s law for our people, for an Israelite who steals and sells his own brethren. Exodus 21:16 is the same judgment for every man, the other nations included.

“If any man have an ear, let him hear.” You’ve got ears on your head and you’ve got a brain: let him hear means understand. Then comes the judgment Christ gave: “He that leadeth into captivity”. To see why Christ said this, go back up to verse 7.

“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. The him in this verse is the so-called white man, which started with Rome, Spain and Portugal. The saints are the saints of the twelve tribes of Israel.

“And to overcome them”: overcoming us means they enslaved us and they killed us. “And power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: the white man ruled everybody, and rules everybody now.

Here’s the judgment the King of Kings gave in regard to verse 7: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity”. That is the judgment. “He that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” So we must patiently wait, with faith, for that.

Christ’s judgment in Revelation 13:10 was based upon the law of Moses in Exodus 21:16: he that stealeth a man and selleth him shall surely be put to death. The ones that led us into captivity go into captivity.

sense.text:
“As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies”. The purpose of the King of kings returning is that we should be saved from our enemies. This is the faith and the patience of the saints.

“And from the hand of all that hate us”. Look at the Christians on the screen: Baptists, Catholics, Presbyterians, Anglicans, Protestants, Lutherans, Adventists, Jehovah’s Witnesses. Those are the ones. They would lynch, burn and hang black men after church, with their families there in their suits; that’s what they did. We want to be saved from our enemies, from the hand of all that hate us.

precepts.why:
Didn’t we read that? Go back so they can see the correlation: “And I will set my face against you, and ye shall be slain before your enemies: they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

They that hate us reign over us, and the prophets spoke since the world began that we should be saved from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us.

Some of you Christians might be sprinkled in here. Put their picture of Christ on the screen: in case y’all didn’t know it, this is called hatred.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire”. So you mean to tell me not one Christian read that Christ had white woolly hair, not one in all these centuries, and they decided to give him straight blonde hair?

“And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”: his feet are the same color as your face, your hands, your body. Brass is brown, as if it burned in a furnace, meaning he’s a black man. They have high school educations and college degrees, and not one of them figured out Christ had white wool hair and skin like it burned in the furnace, and they came up with that depiction. Not one. That’s called hatred, all that hate us.

sense.text: What we read was based upon the law, and Revelation 20 goes into it in detail. “And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand.”

“And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years”. You read the devil and Satan and the churches will say, yes, Revelation 12:9, the spiritual demons. Revelation is written as a similitude, as a metaphor, as an allegory.

This dragon is twofold. It’s not just talking about the spiritual demon, though it is that; it’s also talking about his children. “That old serpent”, the serpent from the beginning. “Which is the Devil”: now we understand who that devil is. It ain’t just a spiritual demon; the Satan and the devil are also people on earth, Esau, Edom.

Satan has children on the earth: that’s your friendly neighborhood white man, first and foremost, and any of you Negroes and Latinos that want to obey them. That includes all your religions; all your religions fall under the Pope. “And bound him a thousand years”: he is bound up for a thousand years.

precepts.why: The churches go here: “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.” You read that and say, oh yeah, okay, the spiritual demons.

“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan came before the Lord, so we know that one is the spiritual demon Satan. We know that one; we’re good with that. But that is not the only Satan the Bible speaks of.

Nobody ever connects this one; they don’t see it in church. “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” They are the synagogue of Satan.

So how come nobody ever connects Revelation 12:9 and Revelation 20:2 with that verse? The Satan there is a people on the earth, the ones who say they are Jews and are not.

Keep reading: “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”. Who’s going to cast us into prison? The devil. The devil casting us into prison, that was Rome.

First John 3:10 is heavy: “In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother.”

Has the white man done righteousness in this earth? Not a damn thing. Does he love us as his brother Jacob? No, he does not. They are the children of the devil.

This isn’t dealing with all people; it’s dealing with Esau. And somebody could say, First John 3:10 talks about black people too. Yes: the black man and black woman that follow Esau, their lies and their customs, fall in that too.

Remember the Pharisees, which were our people, obeyed Rome to the T. Christ said to them: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning”.

Wait a minute: was he talking about the spiritual demon Satan, a spirit in heaven that got kicked out, like the pastor said? Go to Genesis 4 and see who he was, the murderer from the beginning.

“And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Now go back to John 8:44: “He was a murderer from the beginning”. Christ isn’t talking about that spiritual one there; he’s talking about Cain. Cain was a child of Satan.

How do we know Cain was one of the sons of Satan? Read the verses before. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” God said, if you obey my law, won’t you be accepted, Cain?

“And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door”: if you disobey my commandments, Cain, sin lies at your door. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: Satan shall be Cain’s desire, meaning Cain will desire the will of Satan; he will obey Satan. “And thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over Cain. Then Cain rose up against Abel his brother and slew him.

With that understanding, go back to Revelation 20: the dragon, that old serpent, the Devil and Satan, is the spiritual demon and his children on the earth.

sense.text:
“And cast him into the bottomless pit”. Write this down: the bottomless pit is Europe, the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia. There’s no natural resources up there. It’s the same pit you read about in Job 30, where they were chased into the mountains, the cliffs of the rock: same place.

“And shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more”. He deceives the whole world through his media, his religions, his politics, his school system; when he’s shut up, he’s going to deceive the nations no more.

“Till the thousand years should be fulfilled”: for a thousand years these people are shut up in the prison, like the Bible says. Give me Bible? We’re giving you Bible. This is the faith and the patience of the saints. And if it’s not the way the Bishop is breaking it down, you that say he’s taking it out of context, he’s racist, he’s evil: get your scholars, your top apologetics, you people who say you rightly know how to break the Bible down, and explain it to us.

“And after that he must be loosed a little season”: we’re not going to touch on that today; we’ve touched it before.

precepts.why:
See the correlation with “that he should deceive the nations no more”. “And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: what did he do? “Which deceiveth the whole world”. You might say, how does this white man deceive everybody? He deceives the whole world through his media, his religions, his politics, his school system.

Come back to it after Job 9 and 1 Maccabees 3 and we’ve got a better understanding: he deceived the whole world through his media, his school system, his church system, his political system. Everybody’s deceived. You already know the spiritual demon Satan is operating in people; he operates in the white man too, in fact he operates in them so bad that they’re his children on earth. All their media systems work together to deceive the whole world. So when the Bible talks about “the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”, it’s also talking about the white man.

Here are some examples of how they deceive the world. “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked”: who rules the earth? The wicked.

“He covereth the faces of the judges thereof”: like you see right there on the screen, they have a whole conspiracy to cover up the black rulers of Russia, of Europe, the black Israelites, covering all their images up with European images.

“If not, where, and who is he?” In case you want to argue, Christian black man and black woman, Latin man and Latin woman: you tell us who’s ruling the earth. You tell us who’s covering the faces of the judges. We’re going to come to the same conclusion: it’s your friendly neighborhood white man.

“And laid open the book of the law”: the book of the Lord, the Holy Bible, “wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The heathen are the Greeks, the white man. This is what they did throughout our books: when they got our records, they painted the likeness of their images in our records. That is how he deceives the nations.

Where is he going to be bound at? Write this down, for you Christians who say it’s just the spiritual demon Satan and the Bishop don’t know what he’s talking about: compare spiritual things with spiritual, precept upon precept, rightly dividing the word of truth.

“Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth.” “He who fleeth from the noise of the fear”, meaning the destruction, “shall fall into the pit”. “And he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit”, like when they come up out of those underground bunkers, “shall be taken in the snare”. “For the windows from on high are open”: God’s blessings shall be opened up on the Israelites. “And the foundations of the earth do shake”: there’s going to be destruction.

“The earth is utterly broken down”: it’s going to be so bad. “The earth is clean dissolved, the earth is moved exceedingly.” “The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard”: that’s how bad the destruction is going to be when the bombs hit and Christ hits this earth. “And shall be removed like a cottage; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again”: this kingdom shall not rise again.

“The Lord shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high”: the host of the high ones is the so-called white man. He’s the high nation on earth; that’s why they call this place Babylon the great. They’re the greatest ones right now, they’re the high ones. “And the kings of the earth upon the earth”: that’s the EU, NATO, all of them.

“And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited.” That is Revelation 20:3: cast into the bottomless pit and shut up, and for a thousand years these people are shut up in the prison.

sense.text:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them”. Let’s talk about thrones. I know it’s hard for some of y’all to accept that we’re going to have thrones and we’re going to sit on them, and it won’t be a Game of Thrones. It’s not spiritual; it’s physical. It’s hard for a child to see us black men sitting on thrones of rulership, because even on TV they see Superman, Batman, and that’s when they don’t see us. Y’all thought drug dealers, basketball players, musicians, rappers that did evil get put in a position of power. You’re not thinking that the God, the creator of the heavens and earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, created you to be kings to rule on thrones.

“And judgment was given unto them”. You might say, what is the judgment that’s given to them that sat on the thrones? Power. The judgment that’s going to be given to us is power.

precepts.why:
We’re talking about thrones. “Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons”: this is the mother of James and John. “What wilt thou?” What do you want? “Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom.”

“Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of”: what was the cup that Christ had to drink? Death. Are you able to sacrifice yourself like I have to? “And to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with”: the baptism he got baptized with was death. And not no regular death, not a heart attack, not he died from asthma; a horrible death, as Isaiah 52 shows.

“They say unto him, We are able”: James and John said we’re able. “Ye shall drink indeed of my cup”: he said that because Christ knew that they would be put to death.

“But to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give”: I don’t have that power to allow that. “But it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father”: it’s already been prepared who’s going to sit on Christ’s right hand and who’s going to sit on the left. That’s not Christ’s choice, his judgment; it’s only the Father’s.

The cup of Matthew 20:22 was a horrible death. “Behold, my servant shall deal prudently”: wisely. “He shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high”: why? Because he’s the king.

“As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man”: his appearance, his face, was so marred more than any man, more than Emmett. “And his form more than the sons of men”: his body. “So shall he sprinkle many nations”: scattered in many nations. So it says Christ was marred more than any man on earth.

“For that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider.” Nobody ever thought that this was a black man that was brutalized like this, and the kings of the earth are going to realize that they’ve been lied to. People think we’re crazy right now; people say don’t listen to them in purple, they don’t know the Bible, they’re making things up, they’re taking things out of context. Y’all got to find out who’s right and who’s wrong.

He’s talking to the twelve; pay attention to this. “That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration”: the regeneration means coming back all the way up into the kingdom, “when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory”. Here’s the point: “ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

We’re still talking about thrones. “To him that overcometh”: overcome what? His sins, this world. “Will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.” See that: Christ sits with his Father in his throne, and he grants us to sit with him in his.

“Behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone”. Look them up: many of us have never seen those types of stones, and if you’re on the street teaching, most black people don’t know what a sardine or a jasper stone even looks like. The jasper and the sardine stones are brown stones. It’s giving you the complexion of the Almighty God, the Father.

“And there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald”. Put a real rainbow on the screen. You know why that’s important? Christians teach and say there’s no color in heaven; then how the hell was there a rainbow? Lie, lie, lie, you lying Christians.

“And round about the throne were four and twenty seats”: these are the elders of Israel. “Upon the seats I saw four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold.” Twenty-four elders, and of them, twelve is the top. Understand this order is a ranking order.

You might say, how do you know that’s the Father sitting on the throne? Chapter five is going to explain. “And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals”: this is the Holy Bible.

“Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof? And no man in heaven, nor in earth, neither under the earth”, their bodies were dead, “was able to open the book, neither to look thereon”: they couldn’t even look at the words on the page. “And I wept much, because no man was found worthy to open and to read the book, neither to look thereon”: there was nobody worthy to open it and read it, neither to look thereon to get the understanding.

“Weep not”: don’t cry, young man. “Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof”: only Christ could open the book.

“And I beheld, and, lo, in the midst of the throne”: this is how you know the man sitting on the throne was not Christ. Christ came to take the book and to open the seven seals, so the man sitting on the throne was the Father. “Stood a Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God sent forth into all the earth”: that’s the angels. “And he came and took the book out of the right hand of him that sat upon the throne”: Christ approached the throne and took the book out of the hand of the Father.

“Golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints”: our prayers go up to heaven, brothers and sisters.

How do you know the book in the right hand of him that sat on the throne in Revelation 5 is the Bible? This is how we know. “But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end”: meaning the Bible would be sealed until the end times. What time are we living in now? The end times. “Many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased”: the white man’s knowledge shall be increased. So now we know that that book is the Bible.

“And he shewed me a pure river of water of life”: that’s the word of God, “clear as crystal”, it’s being taught, “proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb”. The word of God is going to proceed out of the throne of God and of the Lamb; the Lamb is Christ.

“There the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month”: every month there’s going to be laws, statutes and commandments dictated worldwide. “And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations”: the only way the nations are going to be dealt with right is if they obey the laws, the statutes and commandments. Zechariah says if Egypt does not come up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles, what shall happen? No rain.

“And there shall be no more curse”: the curse of Deuteronomy 28, from verse 15 on, is going to be finished; that’s the proof right there. “But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.”

What is the judgment given to them that sat on the thrones? Power. “And the nations were angry”: when Christ returns the nations are going to be angry, not happy. “And thy wrath is come”: God’s wrath has come. “And the time of the dead, that they should be judged”: the dead shall be judged. Remember the scripture in Baruch, ‘Lord hear the prayer of the dead Israelites’.

“And that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great; and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.”

I’m showing you scriptures saying the same thing: the judgment that’s going to be given is power. “Until the Ancient of days came, and judgment was given to the saints of the most High; and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom.” So how are we going to possess the kingdom in these frail, weak, sick bodies? We got power.

Watch this. “He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also”: you know what kind of mighty works the Son of God did. He said you shall do the same works that I’ve done. “And greater works than these shall he do”: you’re going to do greater works than I’ve done. That is the power given to the saints that sit on the thrones.

The scripture that says the books could not contain the works that Christ did: “And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.” There are so many things that Christ did that are not even written in the Bible, and he said we shall do greater works than these.

sense.text:
Remember, judgment is going to be given unto us, and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom. This is how. “In that day shall the Lord defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”: he that is feeble is us, in these weak, sick, flabby bodies. That feeble one shall be as David, “and the house of David shall be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.”

That’s the faith and the patience of the saints. That’s what I’m waiting for right there. We’re gonna do some mighty works, brothers and sisters.

Now you might say to yourself, what do you mean be as David? There was a whole king. David shows it himself in Psalms 18: he that is feeble among you shall be like David.

precepts.why:
The party ain’t over. It’s hard for us to even visualize this. We have never seen a movie or a comic of us doing great things, so we got to visualize it, because it’s written in the Bible.

“But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength”: here is the patience and faith of the saints, they that wait upon the Lord. “They shall mount up with wings as eagles.” What you think that means? Have you ever seen a man fly? Christ said the works that I do you’re gonna do too, and greater.

We saw Neo do it, the white man Keanu Reeves. We seen Christopher Reeve, the white man, as Superman, and Henry Cavill. It’s so hard for us to imagine black men doing that, that’s why we gotta visualize it ourselves; ain’t nobody else gonna do it for us. They be laughing at us and calling us Power Rangers; in that day you’re gonna know what the Power Rangers could do.

The Lord wrote this. We didn’t sit down yesterday and write it: these are ancient records from the hand of God, so ancient there was no such thing as Hollywood, no TV, no DC Comics, no Marvel Comics. This was history written before the white man was even thinking about this stuff.

Let’s look at one of the works Christ did. “And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” He was taken up: he flew up into the heaven. And Christ said what I do, you shall do, and greater.

Watch the movie Glass. In it there is a unit of white people, psychiatrists, whose job was to make men like Samuel Jackson’s character, who had extreme intellect, and Bruce Willis’ character, who had strength, and the one they called the Beast, strong and acrobatic, believe they were not special: that they were ordinary people, they don’t have superpowers, we’re all the same, we’re all equal. They had them sedated, believing they were just regular people. They had to make sure those three did not show their superpowers to the world, so that people would not wake up; because if people see that they are special, it’s going to ignite something within them, they will start to believe, and their innate superpower will be rekindled.

Now read the Bible. “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God”: we don’t want you to believe that, that’s racist, so don’t believe that. “The Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” Above, above, above all people. The psychiatrists’ job was, you’re not above all people, you’re the same like everybody else.

So with us they said no, you guys are not special, you’re not holy, you black people are nothing. That’s what their job is; that’s what Christianity’s job is. That’s why they mock us. The foundation of them humbling us was when they enslaved us, changed Christ from black to white, and made sure it was pushed everywhere and hung up in our houses: a white man sitting in the clouds with another white man with his penis out. That’s what you have in your mind as superior, and you think a negro can never have no connection to God, that we need white folks to save us.

It says saviours shall rise up from amongst us. There was no movie, other than Birth of a Nation that Nate Parker did, that showed a black man saving a black woman or a black child. It’s always the white man that comes to her rescue; we can never do it. If our children get kidnapped the white man gotta save them, cause we’re too stupid and dumb. We don’t see that visualized in the earth.

But now read the Bible: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion.” Another word for saviours is heroes. They shall come up “to judge the mount of Esau”.

This gives another word for saviours. “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” Saviours, saviours, saviours.

This is David speaking, in the spirit of prophecy. This is what it means to be as David.

“For thou wilt save the afflicted people”: we’re the afflicted people. “But wilt bring down high looks”: bring down white folks’ looks. “For thou wilt light my candle: the Lord my God will enlighten my darkness.”

“For by thee I have run through a troop”: one brother is going to be able to run through a troop of at least five hundred men. Right now you can barely get past one; you can’t run down the block. “And by my God have I leaped over a wall”: not climbed over a wall, leaped. You don’t need a ladder, you don’t need a rope, you’re gonna leap over walls.

“He maketh my feet like hinds’ feet”: like a deer, like a gazelle. A gazelle can leap at least fifteen feet and run, and we could barely run one mile an hour, huffing and puffing. “He teacheth my hands to war, so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms”: you ain’t gotta go to karate school, because God’s gonna teach you how to fight. He that is feeble among you shall be like David: that feeble brother gonna be able to break steel with his bare hands. That’s some power.

“That my feet did not slip”: you know when you’re in a fist fight sometimes you slip. David said when I fight my feet ain’t gonna slip; damn, ain’t nobody gonna be swiping my feet from under me.

“I have pursued mine enemies, and overtaken them: neither did I turn again till they were consumed.” I’m not gonna turn back until I’ve defeated all. David is speaking about the resurrected twelve tribes of Israel. “I have wounded them that they were not able to rise”: Israel’s gonna beat them down so bad they ain’t gonna be able to rise again. “Thou hast subdued under me those that rose up against me”: all the nations that rose up against us, we gonna subdue them.

“Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies; that I might destroy them that hate me.” The Bible says I’m gonna give you the necks of your enemies that hate you.

“They cried, but there was none to save them”: the nations gonna cry, brothers and sisters. Cry me a river: I’m sorry, I didn’t know. There’s gonna be nobody to save them. They’re gonna cry “even unto the Lord, but he answered them not.” “Then did I beat them small as the dust before the wind: I did cast them out as the dirt in the streets.” We ain’t gonna play with them.

Don’t forget the thought where it said judgment was given unto the saints: that’s power, and it’s going to be given to us.

“No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.” In church they say no weapon formed against me means your words ain’t gonna hurt me no more, I’m gonna be able to pay my bills. That’s not what it’s talking about. It’s talking about weapons, the inventions the white man got: a bullet ain’t going to do nothing. Like Superman Returns, when the bullet came to Superman’s eyeball. They visualize it for their people, but the Bible visualizes it for our people.

“And every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn”: every tongue that rises against us in judgment, calling us Gentiles, we gon’ condemn them. “This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness is of me, saith the Lord.”

sense.text:
Back to the thought about judgment. “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: power was given unto them.

Now here’s the part nobody wants to talk about: “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”. We all want that power. Everybody rejoices, even online; everybody wants that thing. But you gotta die to get it. A remnant has to die to get that. What do you mean beheaded? Christ said, are you able to drink the cup that I shall drink? You shall surely drink.

precepts.why:
We’re going to talk about the beheaded. “And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.” This is Salome. She danced for King Herod, a lascivious dance, the type of dance that makes dumb negroes make it rain in the club, and it turned him on, so he was so excited.

“And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her. And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison”. So John got his head cut off.

Nobody wants to talk about this. “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church.” The church, as we know, is the twelve tribes of Israel. “And he killed James the brother of John with the sword”: he cut his head off, he beheaded him.

This is why Christ said to James and John, you shall surely drink the cup that I shall drink. Here’s the evidence: James got put to death.

Let’s go into prophecy. “Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify”. That’s why a remnant is going to get killed. “And some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city”.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations”. You will be hated of all nations for his name, through the propaganda being pushed in the earth through the mouth of the dragon.

“And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Many of you Israelites are gonna be offended and betray this truth. That’s why brothers that just teach on YouTube and never hit the streets don’t impress me. It lets me know you are afraid to hit the streets and go face to face, toe to toe. You hide and never show your face and say I’m a prophet. No, you’re not, you’re hiding. You men and women that sit at home and hide, some of you gonna betray us; some of you gonna hate us.

“And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many”: in Christianity and Islam, the popes, the reverends, the imams. “And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold”: iniquity is going to be raised up in this earth like we’ve never seen.

“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” Endure what? The affliction, the persecution, the betrayal. You gotta endure that.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” Through all that persecution the gospel must still be taught. Christ didn’t say go hide in the corner, hide in the cave. He wants the gospel preached.

sense.text: More prophecy. Don’t think that persecution ended with the twelve. “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” There’s going to be an insurrection upon the Israelites that keep the commandments. It was prophesied from the time of Ezra, and Christ prophesied it, and it’s going to happen. You think this great awakening you’re seeing worldwide, the dragon ain’t gonna react? Get your minds focused.
“They shall be like mad men, sparing none”: there’s going to be mobs of people sparing none, “but still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord.”
“For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.” So don’t be too attached to your homes, your houses, your property. Don’t get too attached, sisters.
“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen”: that’s why Christ said he that endures to the end. “And they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

It doesn’t say the days of my trouble: “behold, the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.” So no matter who dies or who lives, the Lord said I’m going to deliver you from the same, because the dead in Christ shall rise first.
“Be ye not afraid neither doubt”: why did he say that? Because doubt and fear go hand in hand. “For God is your guide”.

“And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down”. Why say that? Because we may fall seven times, but we gotta get up, get up, get up.

“And let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: you better put that iniquity in check. Whatever it is, you men, you women, you know and only you know what you’re battling with. Don’t let your iniquities lift up themselves.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins”: you men and you women that are bound in your sins, where there’s no scripture we can give you to help you; that means you’re bound. “And covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns”: the path of righteousness is covered, you can’t even see the path to go, “that no man may travel through”. No man can go through and help you.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” The only thing that can be done with you men and you women bound in your sin is death. That’s what the Bible is saying right there. That’s why he says let not your sins weigh you down, and don’t let them lift themselves up.

precepts.why: Here’s the precept for that verse. Some of y’all think this is a game. “And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed”: a physical war, they’re gonna lay hands on us. The remnant “which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” That is the insurrection upon those that fear the Lord: upon the Israelites that keep the commandments.

“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” That’s what he said in Ezra: the days of trouble are at hand, but I will deliver you from the same.

We always read this. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear”: so now we understand the spirit of fear is unbelief, doubt. That’s why doubt and fear go hand in hand. “But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind”: meaning our mind is clear, our spirit is clear, we are focused, we know the mission at hand, and we must fulfill it.

sense.text:
We are talking about beheading. “I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death”: that’s the white man. And “Hell followed with him”: the hell that follows him is his politics and his religions, that destroy nations.

“Over the fourth part of the earth”: the fourth part of the world is America. A book was put up called ‘The Fourth Part of the World’, ‘an astonishing epic of global discovery, imperial ambition, and the birth of America’. That is for the new people watching, because the churches ain’t teaching us right; it’s only us teaching it.

He was given power to kill with the sword: that’s war. “With hunger”: that’s famine. “With death”: disease. And with the beasts of the earth.

When the fifth seal was opened John saw “the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held.” That includes what we just read about. John the Baptist got beheaded; James got beheaded in Acts 12 and 2. It includes all the apostles and all the myriad disciples that came behind the twelve.
They cried “How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” On them: that white man that dwells on the earth.

“White robes were given unto every one of them”, and they were told “that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.” Their fellowservants is us, you and me. That is the prophecy that goes with what we read in 2 Esdras 16, Matthew 24 and Matthew 23:34.

So the coming of Christ is held back until the fellowservants are fulfilled, and some of us have got to die first. That’s right. And for that to happen we have got to be built up, because if death came today half of y’all would run out of here and the Lord would never see you again. Our faith must be built up to the point where we can endure that.

precepts.why:
“The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” The torment that shall not touch them is the lake of fire, that thermonuclear destruction that’s coming.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: about the beheading, it is talking about the mass tribulation, the beheading, the affliction we have just been reading about. “Their departure is taken for misery”: their departure from this earth is taken as misery, “And their going from us to be utter destruction”: it seems like we got totally destroyed, “but they are in peace.”

“For though they be punished in the sight of men”, kill them, afflict them, “yet is their hope full of immortality.” “And having been a little chastised”: the beheading, the affliction, the tribulation is called being a little chastised, and “they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them”. Because we all say we believe in the Lord, and he is going to say: prove it. Drink the cup that I drink, be baptized with the baptism I was baptized with. Prove yourselves.

“And found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” He is going to receive our death as a burnt offering. So real bad things are going to happen to those of us following the Lord, to prove us. Yes, we’re gonna catch hell.

“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward”. To who? Us-ward: us Israelites. “Not willing that any should perish”, perish in the lake of fire, “but that all should come to repentance.”

So the Lord is being patient with us. Why? Because there is a remnant that must be sealed, that must learn, whose faith must be increased. That is why the souls under the altar are told to rest yet for a little season: the Lord is being patient.

The servants of God, the prophets, “were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented”. That is what was done to those slain for the word of God.

Watch what Paul says to those Israelites that started waking up, which goes for us today: “Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.”

That hasn’t come yet, brothers and sisters, but it is going to come, where we are going to have to resist unto blood. That means death, striving against sin. You see it now in the school system, the transgender and all that going on. It’s only going to escalate. Those are the fellowservants that should be killed as they were.

“Because iniquity shall abound”: sin shall abound. “The love of many shall wax cold”: the world is going to stop even reading God’s word. “But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” We’ve got to endure the iniquity, through rebuking and teaching.

This is going to become a world, a kingdom, of nothing but sin, with only a small remnant of Israel keeping and teaching the commandments. That is the connection to Hebrews 12:4: the resisting unto blood is coming.

“I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints”. The woman here is America. She has killed a lot of our people. Now the next part: “and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”. That’s you men and women that are keeping; that is what makes the distinction between the blood of the saints and the blood of the martyrs of Jesus.

“And when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration.” This woman America is not finished yet.

Watch what it says about America, Babylon the great: “in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth”, from the time of Cain and Abel. This is that same woman. Hers is the blood the souls under the altar cry to be avenged on.

sense.text:
We haven’t seen this come to pass yet. “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded”: we just read about that, the souls under the altar and the beheading of the saints.

“For the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: the witness of Jesus and the word of God is keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus, and confessing him before men in the time of persecution. His name is called the Word of God. These are they that came out of great tribulation.

precepts.why: Revelation 14:12 explains the witness of Jesus and the word of God: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” That is the witness of God and the faith of Jesus that the beheaded held.

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.”

They read that in the churches and everybody confesses, I believe in Jesus, I believe in God, but they don’t know what it’s talking about. It’s talking about what we read in Hebrews 12:4, resisting unto blood. This is the time of persecution, the time of affliction. It ain’t talking about while you’re comfortable, real comfortable. It’s talking about the time of persecution and affliction: will you still confess him before men then?

And the denying is the betrayal of Matthew 24. A lot of people among us are going to betray us.
Back to what we just read: “Ye have not yet resisted unto blood”. That is what confessing Christ before men is talking about: confessing him when it comes to resisting unto blood.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” That is the time Christ is talking about in Matthew 10. “And then shall many be offended”: many of you are going to be offended, “and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.”

So whosoever shall deny me before men: that’s the betrayal. Here today, betrayed tomorrow.

“Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.”

Why would Christ have Paul say this? Because during the time of persecution and affliction there was a separation between the real and the fake. What Paul was doing before was forcing them to call Jesus a curse, to reject the Son of God. That is what Christ was talking about in Matthew 10:33.

There is a difference. It ain’t talking about while you’re in your comfort zone. This comfort zone we’re in right now is to build our faith.

Paul tells what he did when he was persecuting the church: “I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth. Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison”. Remember we read in Revelation 2 that the devil shall cast some of you into prison.

“Having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them. And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”: forced them to blaspheme. “And being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” He went from city to city persecuting us.

That is what 1 Corinthians 12:3 answers: he compelled them to blaspheme, to call Jesus accursed.

Ezra saw “upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs. And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest”: a young man taller than all the nation of Israel, “and upon every one of their heads he set crowns”. We want that; everybody wants crowns.

“These be they that have put off the mortal clothing”: their bodies, their earthly tabernacles, were put off, “and put on the immortal, and have confessed the name of God: now are they crowned”. Confessing the name of God ain’t learning Hebrew; his name is called the Word of God.

“What young person is it that crowneth them, and giveth them palms in their hands?” “It is the Son of God, whom they have confessed in the world.” Not confessed in your comfortability: confessed in your persecution, confessed in your time of affliction. “Then began I greatly to commend them that stood so stiffly for the name of the Lord”, for the word of God.

This changes the whole dynamic of everything. The real ‘no cowards’ are the ones that stand in righteousness for the Most High God, documented by Christ as having stood stiffly for his word. Those are the beheaded “for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God.”

When it says confessing, some of you think you’ve got to learn Hebrew. That ain’t what it’s talking about. “He was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Christ is the Word of God: to confess the name of God is to confess the Son, and those beheaded “for the word of God” died for him.

It says the same thing we just read in 2 Esdras 2. “What are these which are arrayed in white robes?” “These are they which came out of great tribulation”. Which came out: the churches argue it’s going to be a pre-tribulation deliverance, but it says these are they which came out of great tribulation.

This is what we read in 2 Esdras 16 about that great insurrection against those that fear the Lord, and in Revelation 12:17, the dragon wroth with the woman going to make war with the remnant of her seed which keep the commandments of God. They “have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.”

sense.text:
We’re still in verse 4: “which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”. The precept that explains the mark in the hand and the forehead is the woman of Revelation 17, with the golden cup in her hand and the name written on her forehead. Sum it up in one word: sin.

Why is it so confusing? Some read “Come out of her, my people” and say it means don’t partake of a microchip in your arm. It’s clear: it’s sin. In the hand is the cup, that you support; in the forehead, that you believe them sins.

People ask, if it’s sin, why didn’t God just make it plain in Revelation? Revelation is written in similitudes. In Revelation the word sin is only recorded two or three times; everywhere else it calls the sin the mark of the beast. Ezekiel 9 said the mark of God was the commandment, God’s law; Isaiah 8:16 said the seal of God was God’s law. Then you get to Revelation and it says the mark of the beast, and people are confused: is it a computer chip, is it the Visa card? Are you kidding me? Stop it. Once you understand that the same sin from the beginning of time is the same as at the end of time, you’re going to be good; if you think there’s something new going on, you’re all confused.

precepts.why:
“He carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns. And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand”. The key is in her hand.

“Full of abominations”: pause there. In the hand of America, because the woman represents America. She has a cup, and the cup is full of abomination; that covers a lot of things, “and filthiness of her fornication”.

“And upon her forehead”, her mind, “was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT”: Babylon, that’s the United States of America, “THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” Sum up what is in her hand and on her forehead with one word, brothers: sin. That is the mark in the forehead and in the hand of Revelation 20:4.

Deacon Malachiyah brought it. “I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people”: you Israelites, “that ye be not partakers of her sins”. Her sins: that’s the cup in the hand, that’s the words on the forehead. In the cup, you support that thing; in the forehead, you believe them sins.

Some people read that and say come out of her so you don’t partake of a microchip in your arm. It’s clear: it’s sin.

More proof of what is in the forehead and in the hand: sin. “With all deceivableness of unrighteousness”: sum that up in one word, brothers: sin. “In them that perish”: that’s talking about our people, “because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved”: because you did not keep God’s commandments.

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth”, the truth of Christ and the commandments, “but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” What’s the unrighteousness, brothers? Sin. It’s so easy; it’s confusing to some people because the ones creating the confusion are in sin and glorify sin.

Why didn’t God just make it plain? “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” That is why Revelation is written as similitudes: it says similitude. The word sin is only recorded two or three times in Revelation; everywhere else it calls the sin the mark of the beast.

A brother raised 2 Thessalonians 2, that it had to be revealed at a specific time and wasn’t going to be so clear until things happened. You know why the Lord wrote it like that? Because of what Christ said: “Who hath ears to hear, let him hear. And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” Why don’t you speak plain, Lord?

“Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” To them it is not given. Certain people were given understanding to teach for them: that is why the mark of the beast is hidden in similitudes.

sense.text:
This is proof of what the Bishop just said, and the iniquity here is sin. “Let no man deceive you by any means”, because there is a lot of deception right now and a lot of people are confused. “For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first”: we want to be delivered, but you are not going to get delivered until things get bad.

“And that man of sin be revealed”: just what the Bishop told you, someone has to exemplify what sin is, because black people are confused. “The son of perdition”: the son of the devil.

“Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God”: the one pushing everything that goes against God. A lot of you don’t know who it is, and a lot of you will defend the devil that’s on this earth right now. Black people are confused; you don’t know right from wrong.

“So that he as God sitteth in the temple of God”: you put the white man up as your God and get mad when we say no, he is not. “Shewing himself that he is God”, and you glorify him as your God.

“Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things? And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time.” Like the Bishop just said, there was a specific time for the revealing to come.

“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: that is what we read in Revelation, a mystery of iniquity, a mystery of sin: MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, a nation to rise up in the future to push sin to such a high level that it’s clear to you, people of God. This is it. The destruction is coming; this place has got to be destroyed, because a lot of you are comfortable in sin right now, and the people that are supposed to be teaching the Bible are telling you something totally different from what God says.

Why isn’t the Book of Revelation just written plain? Why is it written in parables and similitudes and allegories? Christ answers it: “Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.”

“For this people’s heart is waxed gross”: our people don’t believe God. They are “dull of hearing”, and “their eyes they have closed”: they closed their eyes to God’s law, “lest at any time they should see with their eyes” and “be converted, and I should heal them.”

So his purpose is not to save all Israel. Some of you Israelites got to die; you’re just too damn wicked.
“But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.” Blessed are your eyes, brothers; blessed are your eyes, sisters. The ones keeping the law see and hear what the rest cannot.

precepts.why:
Notice the people pushing that the mark of the beast is something else: they’re not explaining nothing on how to be righteous. They got you afraid of a chip you can’t find in the Bible, and they don’t have no teachings for you on how to be righteous, and they don’t care about that. Look at what they don’t teach: the Sabbath day, your beard, the dietary law, family, marriage, interaction with the world, the political issues that are happening, how they’re brainwashing us with TV. All they have you terrified about is a chip, and that’s a stumbling block.

Malachi 2:7 is what a man of God, a teacher of God, is supposed to be doing: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth.” This is what keeps us from receiving that mark of the beast of sin: a priest speaking to you who teaches the laws of God, not conspiracy theories, not taking you all over the place.

Pay close attention: “he that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” Don’t miss that first sentence. Giving your mind to the law and meditating on it is the foundation; then you seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and are occupied in prophecy.

“He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also.” What are those subtle parables based upon? The law.

“He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.” How is he able to be conversant in dark parables? Because he was meditating on the law. All the hard sayings, all the parables, are based upon God’s laws. That is why Christ spoke in parables and why Revelation is written in similitudes: once you understand that, you’re going to be good, but once you step outside the Bible and go to la la land, you’re going to be lost.

sense.text:
“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. The souls “beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”, which “had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: and what is that mark, in one word? Sin.

“And they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Now, what is going to happen within them thousand years? The prophets tell it, and some of you are going to like it and some of you not.

This is what happens within the thousand years. “I will allure her”: God is going to allure the Israelites that remain, “and bring her into the wilderness”, the wilderness we have gone over many times. “And speak comfortably unto her” means he gives us the law. He’s going to give us the history, he’s going to give us the understanding, all over again.
“As in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt”: as in the days of our youth when we came out of ancient Egypt. Same thing, same way.
“Thou shalt call me Ishi”: write that down, Ishi means husband. “And shalt call me no more Baali.”

“For I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth”. That means the names we got now in this English tongue, the Spanish tongue, all these names we got for the Lord. Whatever name you think you got for the Lord, he said I’m going to take all that away and give you the pure tongue, “and they shall no more be remembered by their name.”

“And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field, and with the fowls of heaven, and with the creeping things of the ground”: the animals, the birds of heaven, the insects. Some of y’all scared of animals, some scared of any kind of insect. He said I’m going to make a covenant with these animals and these insects for you. Even the mouse will pass by the Israelite house and go into other houses, and no roaches: a covenant with every creeping thing.

“And I will break the bow and the sword and the battle out of the earth, and will make them to lie down safely.” There shall be wars no more.

precepts.why:
Here’s the precept for what we just read. “The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid”, the baby goats, “and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.” There’s some beautiful imagery right there: you ain’t got to worry about animals eating your child no more.

“And the cow and the bear shall feed; their young ones shall lie down together: and the lion shall eat straw like the ox. And the sucking child shall play on the hole of the asp”, that’s a snake, “and the weaned child shall put his hand on the cockatrice’ den”, that’s another snake.

“They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain: for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.” Everywhere the law of God touches, there’s going to be peace on earth, and no animal is going to touch us or our children. There’s going to be a covenant with them, the covenant of Hosea 2:18, and that’s all during the thousand year reign.

Here’s another precept that goes with what we just read, the wolf again: “The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the Lord.” The same covenant with the beasts, the same peace in the thousand years.

sense.text: Now what about us? What’s going to happen? “When he was returned, having received the kingdom”: that’s the Lord, the King of kings. “Then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money”, the understanding of God’s word, “that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.” How much have you gained by your understanding? How many people have you brought into this truth?
“Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds”: the understanding you gave has gained ten. “Because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.”
“Lord, thy pound hath gained five pounds.” “Be thou also over five cities.” In the kingdom the faithful servants are set over cities.

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob”: he ain’t having mercy on all people on the planet, he said he’s going to have mercy on Jacob. “And will yet choose Israel”: he will yet choose us as a special people, his holy people above all people on the earth. “And set them in their own land”: he’s going to set us in our own land, not the League of Nations, not the United Nations. “And the strangers shall be joined with them”: the other nations shall be joined unto us, “and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.”

“And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”: you’re about to get that thing right there. Put them chains up, put some chains back up. We’re going to possess them for servants and handmaids; that’s what it’s talking about. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

precepts.why: Here’s the precept to the part where the strangers “shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations”, and take hold “of him that is a Jew”. What are they going to say? “We will go with you”: we will cleave to you, “for we have heard that God is with you.”

The judgment is going to be worse on some nations as opposed to other nations. “But that which ye have already hold fast till I come. And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations”: the Lord said he’s going to give us power if we can endure to the end.

“And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”: we’re going to rule these nations with a rod of iron. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we’re going to break them, “even as I received of my Father.” That is Israel ruling over their oppressors.

“They shall judge the nations”: we’re going to judge the nations, “and have dominion over the people”: we’re going to rule over the people, “and their Lord shall reign for ever”: Christ the King of kings shall reign forever.

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee”: this white man, and the other nations like the Arabs that afflicted us, “shall come bending unto thee”. They’re going to come bending unto us. “And all they that despised thee”, every nation that hated our guts, “shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet.” They’re going to bow, the ones who will call us “The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

“Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee.” See what the New Testament says: he’s going to make them come and worship before our feet. Ain’t no church teaching that.

“Whoso giveth ear unto her”, unto wisdom, God’s law, “shall judge the nations: and he that attendeth unto her shall dwell securely.” Those who keep the law are the ones who judge the nations in that day. I don’t know about you, but I want to dwell securely.

sense.text:
“But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains”: it’s going to be the highest government on the planet earth. You’re going to have to look up to the kingdom of the Lord. “And it shall be exalted above the hills”, above all the other ones.

“And people shall flow unto it”: you’re going to have nations coming. You’re going to have Israelites coming up that we didn’t even know about, that the Lord is going to bring up. Nations are going to flow. We’re going to have the greatest and highest economy on planet earth.

precepts.why:
“And he carried me away in the spirit to a great and high mountain”: the same mountain we just read about in Micah 4:1. “And shewed me that great city”, the great city of Micah 4:1, “the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, Having the glory of God”.

It “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates”, and “the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel” written on them. “The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal”: as long as it is, it’s going to be that high. It’s going to be huge, gigantic.

“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it”: everyone’s going to obey the law. “And the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it”: we’re the kings of the earth that bring their glory into it. “And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it”: this is why our economy is going to be the best, the highest. All wealth is coming to Jerusalem.

“And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth”: this is how you know the other nations are not the kings, because they’re not going to be entering into it, “but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.”

“The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.” Then the same words as Micah: “the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.” Everybody’s going to flow unto it.

sense.text: Remember, we’re still talking about the thousand year reign. “And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways”: they’re going to learn the law, “and we will walk in his paths”. “For the law shall go forth of Zion”: so whoever said the Lord has done away with it, we don’t know what you’re talking about. The law is going to be taught worldwide, “and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.”

“And he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off”: the nations that fall under that rebuke are going to be broken, and some of them are going to be enslaved. “And they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks”, meaningful instruments: “nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.” There ain’t going to be no more war.
“But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid”: none is going to make us afraid.

“For all people will walk every one in the name of his god”: when you are set over ten cities, five cities, you are going to be a god again. Everybody’s going to walk in the name of his god. That’s why in Zechariah the ten men say, we’re going to take hold, we’re going to go with you: because we’re going to be the gods of those cities, “and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.”

“In that day, saith the Lord, will I assemble her that halteth”: we’re the ones that halt, he’s going to assemble us. “And I will gather her that is driven out”: he’s going to gather us, because we’ve been driven out of Jerusalem, “and her that I have afflicted”: God has afflicted us.

“And I will make her that halted a remnant”: he’s going to make us a remnant, “and her that was cast far off a strong nation”: he’s going to make us a strong nation again. “And the Lord shall reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth, even for ever”: the Lord shall reign over us in Mount Zion. So we’re going to rejoice. That’s what the Bible is talking about.

precepts.why: Go back to Luke 19 to see who “all people” walking “in the name of his god” are: “Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds. And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” And to the second: “Be thou also over five cities.” Now you’re over these cities. The faithful servant set over a city is the god of that city, walking in the name of the Lord our God.

“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” Brother, you hear that? You are gods. So when Micah says every one will walk “in the name of his god”, it is speaking of us: set over ten cities, five cities, two cities, you are going to be a god again.
